name: ip_expire
prose: Static function ip_expire(t), the timer handler of an IPv4 fragment queue (t is the timer embedded in the inet_frag_queue of a struct ipq; it runs without caller-held locks). It takes rcu_read_lock and qp->q.lock, with refs = 1. If INET_FRAG_COMPLETE is already set it jumps to the exit path and changes nothing. Otherwise it sets INET_FRAG_DROP and calls inet_frag_kill (which may increase refs). If fqdir->dead is set it flushes the queue with inet_frag_queue_flush and goes to the exit path, without counting statistics. Otherwise it increments IPSTATS_MIB_REASMFAILS and IPSTATS_MIB_REASMTIMEOUT. If INET_FRAG_FIRST_IN is not set, it exits. Otherwise it pulls the head skb out of the queue with inet_frag_pull_head (exit if none), looks up head->dev with dev_get_by_index_rcu(qp->iif) (exit if none), redoes the route lookup with ip_route_input_noref (a non-zero result becomes the drop reason and it exits), and exits without ICMP if frag_expire_skip_icmp(user) is true and the route type is not RTN_LOCAL. Otherwise it unlocks the queue, sends ICMP_TIME_EXCEEDED / ICMP_EXC_FRAGTIME with icmp_send and goes to rcu_read_unlock. On every path it ends by unlocking qp->q.lock (before icmp_send in the ICMP path), calling rcu_read_unlock, freeing head, if non-NULL, with kfree_skb_reason (reason SKB_DROP_REASON_FRAG_REASM_TIMEOUT unless the route lookup supplied one) and dropping refs references with inet_frag_putn.
note: Reviewer 15 right: when fqdir->dead is set the function flushes and exits before the REASMFAILS/REASMTIMEOUT counters (ip_fragment.c:146-152). Reviewer 1 right (COMPLETE queue only puts refs; head stays NULL).

name: mroute_msgsize
prose: Static function mroute_msgsize(unresolved, maxvif) computing the netlink message size for an ipmr route. It starts from NLMSG_ALIGN(sizeof(struct rtmsg)) (12) plus three 4-byte attributes (RTA_TABLE, RTA_SRC, RTA_DST, 8 bytes each), which is 36 bytes, and returns 36 when unresolved is true. Otherwise it adds nla_total_size(4) for RTA_IIF (8), nla_total_size(0) for RTA_MULTIPATH (4), maxvif * NLA_ALIGN(sizeof(struct rtnexthop)) (8 * maxvif), and nla_total_size_64bit(sizeof(struct rta_mfc_stats)) (28 bytes, plus 4 bytes of alignment padding when CONFIG_HAVE_EFFICIENT_UNALIGNED_ACCESS is not set). So the result is 76 + 8 * maxvif with efficient unaligned access and 80 + 8 * maxvif without. It has no side effects.
note: Old prose said 88 + 8*maxvif (stats term 40): wrong. rta_mfc_stats is 24 bytes, nla_total_size_64bit(24) is 28 or 32 (netlink.h:2381-2388). Reviewer 1 right on 76 + 8*maxvif (for efficient unaligned access); reviewer 15 right that 40 is not derivable. Contract removed because the value depends on a kernel config option.

name: ip_mr_init
prose: __init function ip_mr_init() (the packet name ipmr_init does not exist; the slice held only the tail). It creates the mrt_cachep slab cache with KMEM_CACHE (SLAB_PANIC, so a failure panics instead of returning), then registers the pernet subsystem ipmr_net_ops (on error it destroys mrt_cachep and returns that error), registers the netdevice notifier ip_mr_notifier (on error it unregisters the pernet subsystem, destroys mrt_cachep and returns the error), and, only with CONFIG_IP_PIMSM_V2, adds the PIM protocol with inet_add_protocol (on failure it logs, sets -EAGAIN, unregisters the notifier and the pernet subsystem, destroys mrt_cachep and returns -EAGAIN). Finally it registers the rtnetlink handlers with rtnl_register_many (no error check) and returns 0.
note: Name was a placeholder; real function is ip_mr_init (ipmr.c:3329-3358). Prose otherwise correct; added that the cache creation uses SLAB_PANIC.

name: synproxy_tg4
prose: Static function synproxy_tg4(skb, par), the IPv4 SYNPROXY target. It returns NF_DROP (not consuming skb) if nf_ip_checksum fails, if skb_header_pointer cannot read the TCP header at par->thoff, or if synproxy_parse_options fails. For a pure SYN (SYN set, no ACK, FIN or RST) it counts syn_received, builds the options (ECN if ECE and CWR are set, masks them with the target's options, sets the mss and a timestamp cookie or clears the WSCALE/SACK_PERM/ECN options), calls synproxy_send_client_synack, consumes skb with consume_skb and returns NF_STOLEN. For a pure ACK (ACK set, no FIN, RST or SYN) it calls synproxy_recv_client_ack with ntohl(th->seq): on success it consumes skb and returns NF_STOLEN, on failure it returns NF_DROP (skb not consumed here). For any other flag combination it returns XT_CONTINUE with skb untouched.
note: Both reviewer points are already reflected in the packet text (checksum failure -> NF_DROP is a behaviour, not a precondition; failed synproxy_recv_client_ack gives NF_DROP, ipt_SYNPROXY.c:53-58). Tightened.

name: tcp_ack_update_window
prose: Static function tcp_ack_update_window(sk, skb, ack, ack_seq), called with the socket owned by the caller and with snd_una <= ack <= snd_nxt assumed (not checked). It computes nwin from the TCP header window field in host order, shifted left by tp->rx_opt.snd_wscale unless the segment has SYN set (a 16-bit window shifted by at most the maximum window-scale value fits in u32, so the shift does not wrap). If tcp_may_update_window(tp, ack, ack_seq, nwin) holds it sets FLAG_WIN_UPDATE in the result and calls tcp_update_wl, which records ack_seq in tp->snd_wl1; and only if nwin differs from tp->snd_wnd it sets tp->snd_wnd = nwin, clears tp->pred_flags, runs tcp_fast_path_check, runs tcp_slow_start_after_idle_check when the write queue is not empty, and, only when nwin is greater than tp->max_window, sets max_window = nwin and calls tcp_sync_mss(sk, icsk_pmtu_cookie). In every case it then calls tcp_snd_una_update(tp, ack), which adds ack - snd_una to tp->bytes_acked, calls tcp_snd_sne_update (with CONFIG_TCP_AO and an ao_info present, it increments ao->snd_sne when ack < tp->snd_una) and stores ack in tp->snd_una. It returns FLAG_WIN_UPDATE or 0.
note: All three reviewers right: max_window/MSS resync only when nwin > max_window (tcp_input.c:3759-3762); tcp_update_wl sets snd_wl1 only; the shift cannot wrap, so 'may wrap' was wrong.

name: bpf_iter_tcp_resume_listening
prose: Static function bpf_iter_tcp_resume_listening(seq) used by the BPF TCP iterator to resume in the listening hash; no bucket lock is held on entry (listening_get_first takes the bucket lock). It reads find_cookie = iter->cur_sk and end_cookie = iter->end_sk and remembers resume_bucket = st->bucket. If end_cookie is non-zero and find_cookie == end_cookie it increments st->bucket. It then calls listening_get_first (which returns a socket with its bucket lock held, or NULL with no lock held) and sets iter->cur_sk and iter->end_sk to 0. If a socket was returned, st->bucket is still resume_bucket and end_cookie is non-zero, it calls bpf_iter_tcp_resume_bucket with the cookies iter->batch[find_cookie .. end_cookie): that returns the first socket of the remaining bucket whose cookie matches one of those cookies, tried in cookie order. If none matches it releases the bucket lock, increments st->bucket and returns listening_get_first again (a locked socket of a later bucket, or NULL). In all other cases (NULL result, end_cookie == 0, or the first lookup already moved to a later bucket) it returns what listening_get_first returned. A non-NULL result is returned with its bucket's lhash2 lock held.
note: Reviewers right: the old text assumed the bucket lock was already held on entry; it is taken by listening_get_first (tcp_ipv4.c:2631). The no-sk and end_cookie==0 paths return the first lookup result unchanged (3118-3132).

name: bpf_iter_tcp_resume_established
prose: Static function bpf_iter_tcp_resume_established(seq), the same resume logic as the listening variant for the established hash; no bucket lock is held on entry (established_get_first takes the ehash bucket lock). It reads find_cookie = iter->cur_sk and end_cookie = iter->end_sk, remembers resume_bucket = st->bucket, increments st->bucket if end_cookie is non-zero and find_cookie == end_cookie, calls established_get_first (a socket with its ehash lock held, or NULL with none held) and resets iter->cur_sk and iter->end_sk to 0. Only if a socket was returned, st->bucket still equals resume_bucket and end_cookie is non-zero does it search the rest of that bucket, with bpf_iter_tcp_resume_bucket, for a socket whose cookie matches one of iter->batch[find_cookie .. end_cookie), tried in cookie order. If none matches it releases the ehash lock with spin_unlock_bh, increments st->bucket and returns established_get_first again. In every other case (NULL, end_cookie == 0, or the first lookup already moved to another bucket) it returns the result of the first established_get_first call. A non-NULL result is returned with its bucket's ehash lock held.
note: Reviewer 15 right: the cookie search only runs when the returned socket is still in resume_bucket (tcp_ipv4.c:3152). Reviewers 1 and 2 right about the end_cookie==0 and no-socket paths; no lock is held on entry.

name: tcp_v4_send_reset
prose: Static function tcp_v4_send_reset(sk, skb, reason) sending a RST in reply to skb; sk may be NULL or a full or time-wait socket, and the function returns nothing. It returns without sending anything if the packet has RST set, if sk is NULL and the packet's route type is not RTN_LOCAL, if tcp_parse_auth_options reports invalid options, or if the packet has a TCP-AO header and tcp_v4_ao_sign_reset fails; these returns happen before any RCU lock is taken. With CONFIG_TCP_MD5SIG it then takes rcu_read_lock. If sk is a full socket, the MD5 key is looked up on sk and, if there is none, the RST is still sent without an MD5 option. Otherwise, if the incoming packet carries an MD5 option (and sk is NULL or not a full socket), it looks up a listener with __inet_lookup_listener and its key, and sends nothing (jumping to the unlock) if there is no listener, no key, or the MD5 hash of the packet does not match the one it carries. If a key is found it adds an MD5 option to the reply. Without MD5 it may add an MPTCP reset option. It then fills the reply, copies mark/priority/hash from sk (or time-wait fields), sends it with ip_send_unicast_reply on the per-CPU control socket, and increments TCP_MIB_OUTSEGS and TCP_MIB_OUTRSTS. With CONFIG_TCP_MD5SIG the RCU read lock is released on both the sending path and the suppressed-MD5 path. The caller keeps ownership of sk and skb.
note: Reviewer 15 right: a missing MD5 key does not suppress the RST when sk is a full socket, nor when there is no MD5 option in the packet; suppression occurs only in the md5_hash_location branch (tcp_ipv4.c:812-846, key NULL otherwise leaves the RST unsigned). Slice cut the head (function at 740).

name: tcp_update_metrics
prose: Function tcp_update_metrics(sk), called when a TCP session finishes successfully; it takes the RCU read lock itself. It calls sk_dst_confirm(sk) and returns at once, changing no metric, if net->ipv4.sysctl_tcp_nometrics_save is set or sk has no cached dst. Otherwise, under rcu_read_lock: if icsk->icsk_backoff is non-zero or tp->srtt_us is 0, it looks up the metrics block for the address pair without creating one (tcp_get_metrics, which can itself refresh a block older than the metrics timeout via tcpm_check_stamp) and, if a block exists and TCP_METRIC_RTT is not locked, sets its cached RTT to 0; it then unlocks and returns without touching tcpm_stamp or other metrics here. Otherwise it looks up or creates the block (again with the stale-block refresh on an existing one); if none, it unlocks and returns. With a block: TCP_METRIC_RTT (unless locked) becomes tp->srtt_us if the cached RTT is <= srtt_us, else cached - ((cached - srtt_us) >> 3). TCP_METRIC_RTTVAR (unless locked) becomes m = max(|cached_rtt - srtt_us| >> 1, tp->mdev_us) if m >= cached var, else var - ((var - m) >> 2). Then: if tcp_in_initial_slowstart(tp), SSTHRESH is set to cwnd >> 1 if sysctl_tcp_no_ssthresh_metrics_save is clear, the metric is not locked, the cached value is non-zero and cwnd >> 1 exceeds it, and CWND is set to cwnd if not locked and cwnd exceeds the cached value; else if not in slow start and icsk_ca_state is TCP_CA_Open, SSTHRESH becomes max(cwnd >> 1, snd_ssthresh) (if the sysctl allows and not locked) and CWND becomes (cached + cwnd) >> 1 (if not locked); else CWND becomes (cached + snd_ssthresh) >> 1 (if not locked), SSTHRESH becomes snd_ssthresh if the sysctl allows, not locked, cached non-zero and snd_ssthresh is larger, and REORDERING becomes tp->reordering if not locked, the cached value is smaller and tp->reordering != sysctl_tcp_reordering. Finally tm->tcpm_stamp is set to jiffies and the lock released.
note: Reviewer 15 right: tcp_get_metrics calls tcpm_check_stamp for an existing block (tcp_metrics.c:325-331), which can refresh a stale block and its stamp even in the backoff path (via tcpm_suck_dst); the old text said other metrics and the stamp were left unchanged. Reviewer 2 right (REORDERING needs cached < tp->reordering, 448-455). Reviewer 1 already covered.

name: tcp_time_wait
prose: Function tcp_time_wait(sk, state, timeo), which moves sk to a time-wait or dead FIN-WAIT-2 socket; state is TCP_TIME_WAIT or TCP_FIN_WAIT2. It allocates a timewait socket with inet_twsk_alloc on the death row. If that succeeds it copies connection state into it (mark, priority, window scale, entry timestamp, sequence numbers, receive window, timestamp state and offset, tx hash, queue mappings, and IPv6 addresses and flow information for PF_INET6), runs tcp_time_wait_init and tcp_ao_time_wait; tcp_time_wait_init sets tw_md5_key to NULL, and when MD5 is in use and a key is found it stores a kmemdup copy (a kmemdup failure just leaves tw_md5_key NULL; a failure to take the static-key reference triggers WARN_ON_ONCE, frees the copy and leaves it NULL). It computes rto = 4*icsk_rto - icsk_rto/2, raises timeo to rto if smaller, and then, for state == TCP_TIME_WAIT, replaces timeo by TCP_TIMEWAIT_LEN (so the final timeout is TCP_TIMEWAIT_LEN for time-wait and max(timeo, rto) for FIN-WAIT-2). It then calls inet_twsk_hashdance_schedule(tw, sk, hashinfo, timeo); tw must not be accessed afterwards. If the allocation fails it increments LINUX_MIB_TCPTIMEWAITOVERFLOW. In both cases it then calls tcp_update_metrics(sk) and tcp_done(sk).
note: Reviewer 1 right: for TCP_TIME_WAIT the timeout is forced to TCP_TIMEWAIT_LEN, not rto-bounded (tcp_minisocks.c:377-381). Reviewer 2 right: the kmemdup failure returns silently and only the static-key failure warns (tcp_time_wait_init, 310-321). Old text claimed sk was already in TIME_WAIT/FIN_WAIT2; state is just the target state argument.

name: tcpnv_cong_avoid
prose: Static function tcpnv_cong_avoid(sk, ack, acked) of the TCP-NV congestion control; ack is unused and the function returns nothing. It returns immediately, without changing cwnd, if tcp_is_cwnd_limited(sk) is false or ca->nv_allow_cwnd_growth is 0. If the socket is in slow start it sets acked = tcp_slow_start(tp, acked) (which may increase cwnd and returns the number of packets left over) and returns if nothing is left. Then, if ca->cwnd_growth_factor < 0, it calls tcp_cong_avoid_ai(tp, tcp_snd_cwnd(tp) << -cwnd_growth_factor, acked); otherwise it calls tcp_cong_avoid_ai(tp, max(4U, tcp_snd_cwnd(tp) >> cwnd_growth_factor), acked).
note: Reviewer's point (slow start already advances cwnd through tcp_slow_start before tcp_cong_avoid_ai) is in the packet text and matches tcp_nv.c:193-205.

name: tcp_rtx_synack
prose: Function tcp_rtx_synack(sk, req) retransmitting a SYN-ACK; sk is const because listeners are lockless and no lock is required. If READ_ONCE(sk->sk_txrehash) == SOCK_TXREHASH_ENABLED it first stores net_tx_rndhash() in tcp_rsk(req)->txhash (this happens before the send, so it can change txhash even when the send fails). It then calls af_ops->send_synack(sk, NULL, &fl, req, NULL, TCP_SYNACK_NORMAL, NULL) and returns its result. Only when that result is 0 does it increment TCP_MIB_RETRANSSEGS and LINUX_MIB_TCPSYNRETRANS, increment tcp_sk_rw(sk)->total_retrans if tcp_passive_fastopen(sk) holds, fire the tcp_retransmit_synack tracepoint, and increment req->num_retrans. On a non-zero result no counter, req field other than txhash, or tracepoint is touched.
note: Both reviewer points (txhash updated before the send; total_retrans is on sk via tcp_sk_rw, listeners lockless) are already reflected in the packet text and match tcp_output.c:4581-4600.

name: tcp_vegas_cong_avoid
prose: Static function tcp_vegas_cong_avoid(sk, ack, acked) of the TCP Vegas congestion control; it returns nothing. If vegas->doing_vegas_now is 0 it calls tcp_reno_cong_avoid(sk, ack, acked) and returns without touching Vegas state. Otherwise, if ack is after vegas->beg_snd_nxt (once-per-RTT step): it sets beg_snd_nxt = tp->snd_nxt; if vegas->cntRTT <= 2 it calls tcp_reno_cong_avoid; otherwise it takes rtt = vegas->minRTT, target_cwnd = cwnd * baseRTT / rtt and diff = cwnd * (rtt - baseRTT) / baseRTT and does one of: (a) if diff > gamma and the connection is in slow start, cwnd = min(cwnd, target_cwnd + 1) and snd_ssthresh = min(snd_ssthresh, cwnd) (via tcp_vegas_ssthresh); (b) else if in slow start, tcp_slow_start(tp, acked); (c) else (congestion avoidance) if diff > beta, cwnd is decreased by 1 and snd_ssthresh set to min(snd_ssthresh, cwnd), if diff < alpha cwnd is increased by 1, and otherwise cwnd is left unchanged. After any of these three it clamps cwnd to at least 2 and at most tp->snd_cwnd_clamp and sets snd_ssthresh = tcp_current_ssthresh(sk). In both cases of this once-per-RTT step (the Reno one and the Vegas one) it then resets vegas->cntRTT to 0 and vegas->minRTT to 0x7fffffff. If ack is not after beg_snd_nxt, it calls tcp_slow_start(tp, acked) when the connection is in slow start and does nothing otherwise.
note: Reviewers right (cwnd adjustment only when ack passes beg_snd_nxt; snd_ssthresh set in congestion avoidance only when diff > beta, tcp_vegas.c:255-261), both already in the packet text. Corrected: the cntRTT/minRTT reset also happens after the Reno branch (cntRTT <= 2), not only in the three Vegas sub-cases (283-284).

name: udp_v4_early_demux
prose: Function udp_v4_early_demux(skb) returning an enum skb_drop_reason; the caller holds the RCU read lock. It returns SKB_NOT_DROPPED_YET, without touching skb->sk or the dst, if the UDP header cannot be pulled into the linear area (pskb_may_pull), if the packet is multicast and the device has no in_device or ip_check_mc_rcu says we have not joined the group, or if no socket is found (a multicast lookup for PACKET_MULTICAST, a unicast demux lookup for PACKET_HOST, none for other packet types). When a socket is found it sets skb->sk to it (not refcounted) and skb->destructor to sock_pfree, then takes the socket's cached rx dst and validates it with dst_check. If a valid dst remains it attaches it with skb_dst_set_noref; and if the socket is unconnected (inet_daddr == 0) and in_dev was obtained (multicast case) it returns the result of ip_mc_validate_source, which can be a drop reason. In every other case it returns SKB_NOT_DROPPED_YET, including when the socket was matched but has no valid cached dst (skb->sk stays set and no dst is attached).
note: Both reviewer claims right: ip_mc_validate_source's result can be returned and skb->sk is set before the dst check (udp.c:2931-2955). The old text contradicted itself on skb->sk when the cached dst is invalid; fixed.

name: calipso_cache_init
prose: Static __init function calipso_cache_init(). It allocates the global calipso_cache with kcalloc(CALIPSO_CACHE_BUCKETS, sizeof(struct calipso_map_cache_bkt), GFP_KERNEL); if that fails it returns -ENOMEM (calipso_cache is then NULL). Otherwise it initializes every bucket's spinlock, sets its size to 0 and initializes its list head, and returns 0.
note: Prose matches calipso.c:132-149. The old contract was dropped because the function writes the global calipso_cache (rule 4).

name: ip6erspan_tnl_change
prose: Static function ip6erspan_tnl_change(t, p, set_mtu): it copies the parameters *p into the tunnel with ip6gre_tnl_copy_tnl_parm(t, p), then calls ip6erspan_tnl_link_config(t, set_mtu), which re-runs the link configuration and route configuration (including hard_header_len from ip6erspan_calc_hlen); set_mtu only controls whether the device MTU is updated there. It always returns 0.
note: Prose matches ip6_gre.c:2250-2256 (the called helper recalculates header length and route regardless of set_mtu); reviewer's point already in the packet text.

name: __ip6_append_data
prose: Static function __ip6_append_data(sk, queue, cork_full, v6_cork, pfrag, getfrag, from, length, transhdrlen, flags) appending length bytes to the pending queue of skbs; the slice cut its head. It computes mtu (the cork fragment size, or IP6_MAX_MTU for GSO), fragheaderlen, headersize and maxfraglen itself from the cork's route and options. It returns -EMSGSIZE (after ipv6_local_error, and for dontfrag sockets ipv6_local_rxpmtu) if the headers do not fit or the total length exceeds the allowed size. Zerocopy and splice checks: with MSG_ZEROCOPY and data it returns -EINVAL if msg_ubuf differs from the uarg already on the skb, or -ENOBUFS if msg_zerocopy_realloc fails; with MSG_SPLICE_PAGES and data it returns -EPERM when IPV6 HDRINCL is set. Then it adds length to cork->length, and loops placing data into the last skb or into new skbs: a negative computed copy size gives -EINVAL; allocating a new skb gives the error of sock_alloc_send_skb (for example -EAGAIN or -EINTR) when transhdrlen is non-zero, or -ENOBUFS when it is zero and the write memory limit is exceeded or alloc_skb fails; a failing getfrag gives -EFAULT (a new skb is freed, an existing one trimmed back); MSG_SPLICE_PAGES gives -EIO if the copy exceeds the iterator count (WARN) or the error of skb_splice_from_iter; page-fragment refill failure gives -ENOMEM, running out of fragment slots -EMSGSIZE, and zerocopy errors come from skb_zerocopy_iter_dgram. On success it adds the accumulated wmem_alloc_delta to sk->sk_wmem_alloc and returns 0. On any error after cork->length was increased, it aborts the zerocopy uarg reference, subtracts the unconsumed length from cork->length, counts IPSTATS_MIB_OUTDISCARDS, adds wmem_alloc_delta to sk_wmem_alloc, releases a taken timestamp key, and returns the error; skbs already queued stay on the queue for the caller to clean up.
note: Reviewer 15 right: errors of sock_alloc_send_skb are returned when transhdrlen is non-zero (ip6_output.c:1677-1689, 1688-1689). Also the old prose omitted -EMSGSIZE and -ENOMEM, wrongly said mtu etc. were computed by the caller (they are computed here), and said cork->length stays advanced on error (it is reduced by the unconsumed length, 1780-1785).

name: do_ipv6_setsockopt
prose: Function do_ipv6_setsockopt(sk, level, optname, optval, optlen), the IPV6-level setsockopt worker; the caller does not hold the socket lock. The int value val is 0 if optval is a null sockptr or optlen < sizeof(int), otherwise it is copied from optval (-EFAULT if that copy fails). Multicast-routing options are passed to ip6_mroute_setsockopt and its result returned. A first group of options is handled without the socket lock and returns directly: for example IPV6_UNICAST_HOPS, IPV6_MULTICAST_LOOP/HOPS, IPV6_MTU, IPV6_MINHOPCOUNT, IPV6_RECVERR, IPV6_MTU_DISCOVER, IPV6_ADDR_PREFERENCES (result of ip6_sock_set_addr_preferences), IPV6_MULTICAST_IF (-ENOPROTOOPT on a stream socket, -ENODEV for an unknown device index, -EINVAL on a bound-device mismatch) and IPV6_UNICAST_IF (-EADDRNOTAVAIL for an unknown device, -EINVAL if the socket is bound to a device); these return 0 or -EINVAL for short optlen or out-of-range values (IPV6_MULTICAST_HOPS on SOCK_STREAM returns -ENOPROTOOPT). All other options run after sockopt_lock_sock; if the socket was concurrently converted away from AF_INET6 the result stays -ENOPROTOOPT, which is also the initial result and the result for an unknown optname. Options in this group include IPV6_ADDRFORM (conversion to IPv4: -EINVAL for a value other than PF_INET or a short optlen, -ENOPROTOOPT for raw sockets and protocols other than UDP/UDPLITE/TCP, -EBUSY for a pending UDP send or a non-v6 TCP protocol, -ENOTCONN if not established, -EADDRNOTAVAIL if the peer is not a v4-mapped address), the receive-info bit options, IPV6_TRANSPARENT (-EPERM without CAP_NET_RAW or CAP_NET_ADMIN), sticky packet options and IPV6_2292PKTOPTIONS (-EINVAL, -ENOBUFS, -EFAULT), membership and anycast joins (-EPROTO on an inet connection socket, -EFAULT for failed copies), IPV6_ROUTER_ALERT, IPV6_FLOWLABEL_MGR, and IPV6_IPSEC_POLICY/XFRM_POLICY (-EPERM without CAP_NET_ADMIN). A short optlen or out-of-range value gives -EINVAL through the e_inval label. Results of helpers (for example ipv6_sock_mc_join, ipv6_sock_ac_join, ipv6_flowlabel_opt, xfrm_user_policy) are returned as the result. The lock is released before returning in every locked path.
note: Reviewer 1 right (the function takes the lock itself, ipv6_sockglue.c:549-555, 278-281 offset). Reviewer 2 right (-ENOPROTOOPT is the initial result, 382). The listed errors are summarized by option group rather than per option; each named errno was checked against the code, but I did not enumerate every option. Slice cut the head (function at 377).

name: ndisc_router_discovery
prose: Static function ndisc_router_discovery(skb) processing a received IPv6 router advertisement; it returns an skb drop reason (SKB_DR) which is SKB_CONSUMED only when the neighbour entry was updated, and the default 'not consumed' value on the quiet exits; the packet slice held only the middle of it. It returns early: the default reason if the source is not link-local, there is no inet6 device, or (in some configs) the node type says the sender is a host; SKB_DROP_REASON_PKT_TOO_SMALL if the option length is negative; SKB_DROP_REASON_IPV6_NDISC_BAD_OPTIONS if ndisc_parse_options fails. If ipv6_accept_ra is false it skips the link-parameter step. Otherwise (and unless the node type is NODEFAULT) it records IF_RA_RCVD if an RS was sent, copies the managed/other-config flags from the RA into the device flags, and, if accept_ra_defrtr is set, handles the default route: it skips the default route if the router lifetime is non-zero but below accept_ra_min_lft or if the source is a local address while accept_ra_from_local is off; it finds the existing default router and its neighbour (returning without consuming if the neighbour is missing), deletes the route if lifetime is 0 or the metric differs from ra_defrtr_metric, adds a default router with rt6_add_dflt_router when none remains and lifetime is non-zero (returning if that fails or has no neighbour), updates the preference of an existing route, sets the route expiry and gc list, and may update the hop limit if it passes accept_ra_min_hop_limit. It then updates the retransmit and reachable timers from the RA. After skip_linkparms it looks up or creates the neighbour entry (if none yet) and calls ndisc_update with the source link-layer address (jumping to out if that address has an invalid length) and sets the reason to SKB_CONSUMED. If accept_ra is off it goes to out. Otherwise it processes route-info options (with CONFIG_IPV6_ROUTE_INFO, subject to the length and prefix filters), skips the rest for NODEFAULT senders, processes prefix-information options, an MTU option (updating ra_mtu and, if valid, cnf.mtu6 and rt6_mtu_change), and user options. At out it sends an RTM_NEWLINK notification if flags, timers or ra_mtu changed, releases the route and the neighbour references and returns the reason.
note: The packet item was an unnamed fragment; the code is ndisc_router_discovery (ndisc.c:1230-1597). The old prose was generic; this summary was written from the full function, grouping steps rather than listing every sysctl check.

name: fib6_ifdown
prose: Static function fib6_ifdown(rt, p_arg), a fib walker callback called with the write lock of rt's table held; p_arg is a struct arg_netdev_event with dev and event. It returns 0 if rt is the null entry or has a nexthop object (rt->nh). NETDEV_UNREGISTER: returns -1 if rt's nexthop device is dev, else 0. NETDEV_DOWN: returns -1 if rt->should_flush; for a route without siblings returns -1 if its nexthop device is dev, else 0; for a route with siblings, if rt6_multipath_uses_dev(rt, dev) it counts dead nexthops (those on dev or already RTNH_F_DEAD): if all nexthops including rt are dead it calls rt6_multipath_flush (setting should_flush on the group) and returns -1; otherwise it sets RTNH_F_DEAD | RTNH_F_LINKDOWN on the nexthops using dev, updates the sernum and rebalances. For any route with siblings that is not flushed (including one that does not use dev at all) it then returns -2. NETDEV_CHANGE: if rt's nexthop device is dev and rt has neither RTF_LOCAL nor RTF_ANYCAST it sets RTNH_F_LINKDOWN on rt's nexthop, rebalances the multipath, and falls through to return 0. Any other event returns 0.
note: Reviewers right: for a multipath route the code returns -2 even when rt6_multipath_uses_dev is false (route.c:4992-5005), and the all-dead multipath case returns -1 (4996-4999); the old text did not separate the cases cleanly.

name: seg6_chk_next_csid_cfg
prose: Static function seg6_chk_next_csid_cfg(block_len, func_len) checking that Locator-Block and Locator-Node Function lengths (in bits, u8 values) fit a C-SID container. It returns -EINVAL (-22) if block_len + func_len exceeds 128, if block_len is 0, greater than 120 or not a multiple of 8, or if func_len is 0, greater than 120 or not a multiple of 8, and 0 otherwise. It has no side effects.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures result == ((block_len + func_len > 128 || block_len == 0 || block_len > 120 || (block_len % 8) != 0 || func_len == 0 || func_len > 120 || (func_len % 8) != 0) ? -22 : 0); */
note: Matches seg6_local.c:2106-2127 with the macros in include/net/seg6_local.h:100-110, where the block/function checks also reject lengths above 120 (the old text omitted it; with the sum <= 128 and the other length >= 8 it is implied, but it is stated now). The contract now includes the -22 result.

name: iucv_sock_close
prose: Static function iucv_sock_close(sk) closing an AF_IUCV socket; the caller does not hold the socket lock. It takes lock_sock(sk) and releases it before returning. By sk_state: IUCV_LISTEN: iucv_sock_cleanup_listen dequeues every non-accepted child, closes and kills it, and sets the parent's state to IUCV_CLOSED; the IUCV path is not severed. IUCV_CONNECTED: for the HIPER transport only it first sends an AF_IUCV_FLAG_FIN control message with iucv_send_ctrl and sets the state to IUCV_DISCONN; for other transports no FIN is sent. It then continues as for IUCV_DISCONN: state becomes IUCV_CLOSING, and if no FIN error occurred and iucv->skbs_in_xmit > 0 it waits (sk_lingertime if SOCK_LINGER is set and non-zero, otherwise IUCV_DISCONN_TIMEOUT) for the state to become IUCV_CLOSED. Then, as for IUCV_CLOSING (which is entered directly, without the wait): state IUCV_CLOSED, sk_err = ECONNRESET, state-change callbacks, send_skb_q and backlog_skb_q purged, and iucv_sever_path(sk, 1) called. For any other state (for example IUCV_OPEN) only iucv_sever_path(sk, 1) is called and sk_state is left unchanged. Then, if iucv->hs_dev is non-NULL, it releases that device reference, sets hs_dev to NULL and sk_bound_dev_if to 0; finally it sets SOCK_ZAPPED so iucv_sock_kill can destroy the socket.
note: Reviewer 1 right (default state leaves sk_state unchanged); reviewer 2 right (LISTEN does not sever the path); reviewer 15 right that only the FIN step is HIPER-specific, non-HIPER IUCV_CONNECTED still goes through CLOSING/CLOSED, purge and sever (af_iucv.c:409-441). Slice did not contain the definition at 396 (name outside slice).

name: kcm_sendmsg
prose: Static function kcm_sendmsg(sock, msg, len) of the KCM socket; it takes kcm->tx_mutex and then lock_sock(sk), and releases both before returning on every path. eor is derived from the socket type: for SOCK_DGRAM it is !(MSG_MORE), otherwise MSG_EOR. It first goes to the error path with err = -EPIPE if sk->sk_err is set. If there is a partially built message (kcm->seq_skb) it continues it. Otherwise, if the socket has no sndbuf space it pushes pending data and waits (sk_stream_wait_memory), going to the error path on a wait error; with data to send it allocates a head skb (waiting for memory in a loop). It then copies data into page fragments (or splices pages with MSG_SPLICE_PAGES), chaining extra skbs when MAX_SKB_FRAGS is reached; running out of memory pushes and waits, other copy errors go to the error path. When all data is copied: with eor, a head skb (if any) is queued on sk->sk_write_queue, kcm->seq_skb is cleared and tx_msgs counted; with MSG_BATCH it sets tx_wait_more, otherwise, if tx_wait_more was set or the queue was empty, it calls kcm_write_msgs and only reports a hard error on the socket (report_csk_error), without changing the return value. Without eor the head and last skb are saved in kcm->seq_skb. It then adds the copied bytes to the statistics and returns copied (the number of bytes accepted). Error path: kcm_push is called; a just-added empty frag skb is removed; for SOCK_SEQPACKET, if some bytes were already copied the partial message is saved in kcm->seq_skb and copied is returned (partial success); if none were copied, kcm->seq_skb is left as it was and head is freed only if it is not kcm->seq_skb; for other socket types head is freed and kcm->seq_skb is cleared. The returned error is sk_stream_error(sk, flags, err), derived from -EPIPE, -EAGAIN, -EINTR or a copy error, and sk_write_space is called if the write queue is empty and the error is -EAGAIN.
note: Reviewer 15 right: for SOCK_SEQPACKET with copied == 0 kcm->seq_skb is not cleared and head is freed only if different from it (kcmsock.c:956-963); the old prose said the head was freed and seq_skb cleared on every error. Slice did not contain the head of the function (at 751).

name: pfkey_compile_policy
prose: Static function pfkey_compile_policy(sk, opt, data, len, dir) building an xfrm policy from a socket option's PF_KEY policy data; the packet name pfkey_msg2xfrm_policy does not exist. It always writes *dir. It returns NULL with *dir = -EOPNOTSUPP if sk is AF_INET and opt is not IP_IPSEC_POLICY or (with IPv6) sk is AF_INET6 and opt is not IPV6_IPSEC_POLICY, and NULL with *dir = -EINVAL for any other socket family. It returns NULL with *dir = -EINVAL (nothing allocated) if len < sizeof(struct sadb_x_policy), sadb_x_policy_len*8 > len, the policy type is above IPSEC_POLICY_BYPASS, or the direction is 0 or above IPSEC_DIR_OUTBOUND; NULL with *dir = -ENOBUFS if xfrm_policy_alloc fails. Otherwise it sets the action to XFRM_POLICY_BLOCK for IPSEC_POLICY_DISCARD and XFRM_POLICY_ALLOW for the others, infinite soft and hard byte and packet limits, family from sk->sk_family, xfrm_nr 0; for IPSEC_POLICY_IPSEC it parses the requests with parse_ipsecrequests (a negative result is the error). If the data holds a following security context it checks its length (-EINVAL if truncated), verify_sec_ctx_len (non-zero result is the error) and security_xfrm_policy_alloc (non-zero result is the error). On any of these failures it sets xp->walk.dead, destroys the policy with xfrm_policy_destroy and returns NULL with *dir set to the error. On success it sets *dir = sadb_x_policy_dir - 1 and returns the new policy, which the caller owns.
note: Name was wrong; the function is pfkey_compile_policy (af_key.c:3283-3352). The old prose omitted the socket family / opt check with -EOPNOTSUPP and -EINVAL and did not describe the security-context step's order precisely. No reviewer claims beyond the mechanical name one.

name: llc_proc_init
prose: __init function llc_proc_init(). It creates the directory "llc" under init_net.proc_net with proc_mkdir; if that fails it returns -ENOMEM. It then creates the seq files "socket" and "core" (mode 0444) in it; if creating "socket" fails it removes the "llc" directory and returns -ENOMEM; if creating "core" fails it removes "socket" and the "llc" directory and returns -ENOMEM. On success it returns 0. It stores the directory in the static llc_proc_dir.
note: Matches llc_proc.c:219-244. The old contract was dropped because the function writes the static llc_proc_dir (rule 4); the earlier mechanical rejections concerned that contract.

name: __ieee80211_start_rx_ba_session
prose: Function __ieee80211_start_rx_ba_session(sta, dialog_token, timeout, start_seq_num, ba_policy, tid, buf_size, tx, auto_seq, addba_ext_data), which handles an incoming ADDBA request; the caller holds the wiphy lock (asserted) and the function returns nothing. It computes a status, initially WLAN_STATUS_REQUEST_DECLINED, and ends by recording success state and, if tx is true, sending an AddBA response with ieee80211_send_addba_resp (dialog token, tid, status, the final buf_size, timeout, addba_ext_data). Declined (status stays REQUEST_DECLINED): tid >= IEEE80211_FIRST_TSPEC_TSID; a station with no valid_links and no HT, HE or S1G support; WLAN_STA_BLOCK_BA set; an existing session with the same dialog token whose timeout differs or which has no tid_rx; any memory allocation failure; a failing drv_ampdu_action. INVALID_QOS_PARAM: ba_policy != 1 and (valid_links is set, or the HT cap lacks IEEE80211_HT_CAP_DELAY_BA, or the S1G cap lacks S1G_CAP3_HT_DELAYED_BA), or the requested buf_size exceeds max_buf_size (EHT value if valid_links or EHT, else HE, else HT). After these checks a zero buf_size becomes max_buf_size and it is clamped to sta->sta.max_rx_aggregation_subframes. If agg_session_valid is set for tid with the same dialog token, the status is SUCCESS only when the existing session's timeout equals timeout, and nothing else is done; with a different dialog token the existing Rx session is first stopped with __ieee80211_stop_rx_ba_session, even if this request is later declined. If the hardware supports a reordering buffer it calls drv_ampdu_action and the status is SUCCESS if that returns 0, with no software session allocated and no timer. Otherwise it allocates the session and its reorder buffers (freed again on allocation or driver failure), calls drv_ampdu_action, fills the session, sets SUCCESS, publishes it with rcu_assign_pointer in sta->ampdu_mlme.tid_rx[tid] and, if timeout is non-zero, arms session_timer and sets last_rx. On every SUCCESS it sets agg_session_valid for tid, clears unexpected_agg for tid and stores the dialog token in tid_rx_token[tid].
note: Prose checked against agg-rx.c:271-466; reviewers' points (success without a software session on the hardware-reorder path or duplicate, a decline may already have stopped an existing session, response only if tx, timer only on the software-session path) are all right and stated.

name: ieee80211_stop_tx_ba_session
prose: Function ieee80211_stop_tx_ba_session(pubsta, tid) asking mac80211 to stop a TX aggregation session. It returns -EINVAL, without taking sta->lock, if the driver has no ampdu_action op or tid >= IEEE80211_NUM_TIDS. Otherwise it takes sta->lock with BH disabled; if there is no TX aggregation state (tid_tx) for tid it returns -ENOENT. If a session exists it issues a WARN if sta->reserved_tid == tid; if HT_AGG_STATE_STOPPING is already set it returns 0 without queueing anything; otherwise it sets HT_AGG_STATE_WANT_STOP on the session, queues sta->ampdu_mlme.work on the wiphy and returns 0. sta->lock is released on every path that took it.
note: Matches agg-tx.c:868-904; both reviewer points (TID range and driver support are checked, STOPPING path does not queue) are right and already in the packet text. Slice did not contain the definition (name outside slice).

name: ieee80211_calc_expected_tx_airtime
prose: Function ieee80211_calc_expected_tx_airtime(hw, vif, pubsta, len, ampdu) estimating the transmit airtime in microseconds of a frame; the slice held only its tail. It adds 38 bytes for the Ethernet header to len and reads vif->bss_conf.chanctx_conf with rcu_dereference, so the caller must hold the RCU read lock (it neither takes nor releases it); if the channel context exists it takes its band, otherwise band stays 0. If pubsta is non-NULL it fills an RX status from the station's last TX rate and returns 0 if that fails; for a legacy encoding, or when ampdu is false, it returns ieee80211_calc_rx_airtime for that status and len; otherwise it takes the rate duration and overhead, chooses an aggregation shift from the duration, computes duration * len / AVG_PKT_SIZE / 1024 + (overhead >> agg_shift) and returns it, at least 4. This pubsta path returns before the channel context is checked, so a missing chanctx does not give 0 there. If pubsta is NULL it returns 0 when there is no channel context; otherwise it takes the lowest configured basic rate of the vif (index 0 if none is set) with the short-preamble setting and returns ieee80211_calc_legacy_rate_duration for len.
note: Reviewer 15 right: the pubsta path returns before the !conf test (airtime.c:777-815 vs 817-818). Old prose also claimed the function takes the RCU lock internally; it only uses rcu_dereference, so the caller must hold it. Name was a placeholder; real function at airtime.c:756.

name: __ieee80211_request_smps_mgd
prose: Function __ieee80211_request_smps_mgd(sdata, link, smps_mode) handling a request to change the spatial multiplexing power-save mode of a station interface; the wiphy lock is held (asserted). It warns once and returns -EINVAL if the interface type is not NL80211_IFTYPE_STATION. It returns 0 without changing anything if the link is not active. Otherwise it saves old_req = link->u.mgd.req_smps and stores smps_mode, unresolved (even IEEE80211_SMPS_AUTOMATIC), into link->u.mgd.req_smps, and returns 0 without sending a frame if the driver set IEEE80211_VIF_EML_ACTIVE, if the old request equals smps_mode and it is not IEEE80211_SMPS_AUTOMATIC, or if the interface is not associated or the operating channel width is NL80211_CHAN_WIDTH_20_NOHT. Otherwise it looks under RCU for an authorized, uploaded TDLS peer station of sdata; for IEEE80211_SMPS_AUTOMATIC it resolves a local mode: OFF if such a peer was found or powersave is off, else DYNAMIC. It sends an SMPS action frame to the AP with ieee80211_send_smps_action (link_id for an MLD vif, -1 otherwise). On failure it restores link->u.mgd.req_smps to old_req and returns the error; on success, if the resolved mode is not OFF and a TDLS peer was found, it calls ieee80211_teardown_tdls_peers(link); it returns 0.
note: Prose matches cfg.c:3556-3627. Reviewer 1 and 2: the inactive-link and no-send paths return 0 as stated; the stored value is the unresolved smps_mode (3575), and the inactive-link return precedes the store (3571-3575), consistent with the packet text. Slice cut the head (function at 3556).

name: ieee80211_is_scan_ongoing
prose: Static function ieee80211_is_scan_ongoing(wiphy, local, chandef) returning bool; the caller holds the wiphy mutex (it uses wiphy_dereference), and no RCU lock is used. It returns false if local->roc_list is empty and local->scanning is false. Otherwise it gets the radio index of chandef->chan with cfg80211_get_radio_idx_by_chan. If local->scanning is set it reads local->scan_req; if that is NULL it warns once and returns true, else it returns ieee80211_is_radio_idx_in_scan_req for the scan request and that radio index. If not scanning it returns true if any entry of local->roc_list has a channel with the same radio index, and false otherwise. It takes no locks or references.
note: Prose matches cfg.c:3822-3857; both reviewer points (scanning with a NULL scan_req returns true; wiphy mutex rather than RCU is relied on) are right and already in the packet text.

name: _ieee80211_recalc_chanctx_min_def
prose: Static function _ieee80211_recalc_chanctx_min_def(local, ctx, rsvd_for, check_reserved) recomputing the minimal channel definition of a channel context; the wiphy lock is held (asserted). If ctx->conf.def.width is NL80211_CHAN_WIDTH_5, _10, _1, _2, _4, _8 or _16, or ctx->conf.radar_enabled is set, it sets ctx->conf.min_def = ctx->conf.def and returns 0 without any downgrade. Otherwise it gets max_bw from ieee80211_get_chanctx_max_required_bw(local, ctx, rsvd_for, check_reserved), copies ctx->conf.def and downgrades the copy with ieee80211_chandef_downgrade while its width is greater than max_bw. If the copy is identical to the current ctx->conf.min_def it returns 0 without changing it. Otherwise it stores the copy in ctx->conf.min_def and returns 0 if ctx->driver_present is false, else IEEE80211_CHANCTX_CHANGE_MIN_DEF. It takes no lock and transfers no reference.
note: Reviewer right that the early-return case copies def to min_def without downgrading (chan.c:409-420); this was already in the packet prose. Removed the unverified description of what ieee80211_get_chanctx_max_required_bw does with check_reserved. Slice cut the head (function at 399).

name: drv_add_nan_func
prose: Static inline function drv_add_nan_func(local, sdata, nan_func), the mac80211 wrapper for the driver's add_nan_func op. It must be called from a context that may sleep (might_sleep) with the wiphy lock held (lockdep_assert_wiphy) and with sdata present in the driver (check_sdata_in_driver). If local->ops->add_nan_func is NULL it returns -EOPNOTSUPP. Otherwise it records a trace event, calls local->ops->add_nan_func(&local->hw, &sdata->vif, nan_func), traces the int result and returns it unchanged. It takes or releases no locks or references itself.
note: Matches driver-ops.h:1521-1539; the slice cut the head of the function (name outside slice).

name: fils_encrypt_assoc_req
prose: Function fils_encrypt_assoc_req(skb, assoc_data) encrypting the tail of a (Re)Association Request frame with FILS AES-SIV; the packet name fils_encrypt_assoc_resp does not exist and the slice cut the head (function at fils_aead.c:225). It locates the capability and IE fields depending on whether the frame is a reassociation request, and finds the FILS Session extension element in the IEs; if it is missing or its data length is not 9 it returns -EINVAL without modifying skb (it does not check any minimum frame length; that check is in fils_decrypt_assoc_resp). It sets encr to the first byte after the FILS Session element, builds five AAD vectors (STA address, AP address, the two FILS nonces, and the frame from the capability field through the FILS Session element), computes crypt_len as the bytes from encr to the end of skb, extends skb by AES_BLOCK_SIZE with skb_put, and returns aes_siv_encrypt(kek, kek_len, encr, crypt_len, 5, addr, len, encr), which encrypts in place with the SIV tag prefixed (the result is 0 or a negative errno from that helper).
note: Name was wrong and the described -EINVAL for frames shorter than 24+6 bytes belongs to fils_decrypt_assoc_resp, not to the encrypt function (fils_aead.c:225-274 vs 276-290). Prose otherwise correct.

name: __ieee80211_sta_join_ibss
prose: Static function __ieee80211_sta_join_ibss(sdata, bssid, beacon_int, req_chandef, basic_rates, capability, tsf, creator), returning nothing; the wiphy lock is held (asserted). It resets the TSF with drv_reset_tsf, flushes the interface's stations if the BSSID differs from ifibss->bssid, and if the interface was already joined it clears ibss_joined and ibss_creator and enable_beacon, turns the carrier off, notifies the driver of the BSS change and calls drv_leave_ibss. It then frees any old ifibss->presp via kfree_rcu and sets it to NULL. It copies the requested chandef; if beaconing is not allowed on it and its width is 5, 10, 20 NOHT or 20 MHz, or it is still not allowed after downgrading to 20 MHz, it logs and returns. It also returns (logging) if cfg80211_chandef_dfs_required reports an invalid chandef, or reports DFS required while ifibss->userspace_handles_dfs is false, or if ieee80211_link_use_channel fails. On those early returns ifibss->presp is NULL and no beacon is published (ifibss->bssid has not been changed yet and no channel context was taken). After the channel context is obtained it records radar_required and copies the BSSID into ifibss->bssid. If ieee80211_ibss_build_presp fails it returns with ifibss->presp NULL, the BSSID and radar_required updated and the channel context still held. Otherwise it publishes presp, fills in the vif configuration (enable_beacon, beacon interval, basic rates, SSID, slot time, 11g mode, WMM defaults), marks ibss_joined and ibss_creator and calls drv_join_ibss. If that fails it clears ibss_joined, ibss_creator, enable_beacon and ssid_len, sets ifibss->presp to NULL, frees presp with kfree_rcu, releases the channel context and returns. On success it notifies the accumulated BSS changes, sets ifibss->state to IEEE80211_IBSS_MLME_JOINED, arms the merge timer, informs cfg80211 of the BSS (and puts the reference), turns the carrier on and calls cfg80211_ibss_joined.
note: Prose matches ibss.c:211-380; both reviewer points (bssid/radar_required stay updated after a presp-build failure; channel context is released on driver failure) are right and were already in the packet text. Slice cut the head (function at 211).

name: ieee80211_do_stop
prose: Static function ieee80211_do_stop(sdata, going_down) tearing down a mac80211 interface when its netdev goes down; the wiphy lock is held (asserted) and the function returns nothing. It clears SDATA_STATE_RUNNING, cancels a scan owned by this interface, purges remain-on-channel work, and does per-type stop work (station, IBSS, monitor list removal, AP_VLAN link clearing). It flushes all stations of the interface itself with sta_info_flush (it does not require the caller to have done so; it WARNs if stations other than on an AP_VLAN were flushed), adjusts the allmulti, pspoll and probe-request filter counts, removes the interface's multicast addresses, cancels dynamic PS and CSA/CAC/colour-change work (aborting a started CAC and releasing the link channel), and for AP_VLAN removes buffered broadcast packets for this device. If going_down it decrements local->open_count. It then does type-specific cleanup: AP_VLAN (unlist, clear chanctx, free keys), monitor (decrement monitor counts and update the monitor flags), NAN (free all functions), others (cancel the sdata work, free keys, purge skb_queue and status_queue). It unlinks and frees this interface's skbs from local->pending, removes txq state, sets sdata->bss to NULL, clears pending TX if open_count is 0 and sets beacon_int to 0. If local->suspended is set it returns here (after WARNs) without driver teardown. Otherwise, for a monitor interface it deletes the virtual monitor when none remain, recalculates idle and offload state, and (for non-virtual monitors) releases the link channel; for other types except AP_VLAN, when going_down is true it calls drv_remove_interface and clears the vif private data. It then recalculates PS, flushes the scan work if a scan was cancelled and, if open_count is 0, calls ieee80211_stop_device(local, false) and returns; otherwise it reconfigures the filter and hardware and re-adds the virtual monitor if virt_monitors equals open_count.
note: Name was a placeholder; the function is ieee80211_do_stop (iface.c:475-759). Reviewer right: it calls sta_info_flush itself (iface.c:511-512), so the old precondition that the caller already flushed stations was wrong.

name: ieee80211_key_replace
prose: Static function ieee80211_key_replace(sdata, link, sta, pairwise, old, new) replacing or installing a key; the wiphy lock is held (asserted). If both old and new are NULL it WARNs and returns 0. The key index, WEP status and link id come from new, or from old if new is NULL. It returns -EINVAL (with a WARN) if old's link id differs from the link id, and, for link_id >= 0, -ENOLINK if the link (or, with a station, the station's link entry) is absent; it returns -EINVAL if the key is WEP or pairwise and idx >= NUM_DEFAULT_KEYS. For a pairwise key with a station and a new key it calls ieee80211_pairwise_rekey. Hardware: if old exists and was uploaded to hardware it disables old (ieee80211_key_disable_hw_accel) and, if new is present, enables new, keeping that result; if old does not exist, it enables new in hardware unless wowlan is active, in which case, for an active link, it marks new KEY_FLAG_UPLOADED_TO_HARDWARE and calls decrease_tailroom_need_count(sdata, 1) only if new's conf flags lack GENERATE_MMIC, PUT_MIC_SPACE and RESERVE_TAILROOM. If enabling new in hardware failed, it returns that error with nothing installed in the software lists or pointers (old stays in the lists, though it has already been disabled in hardware). Otherwise it appends new (if any) to sdata->key_list; with a station it stores new in sta->ptk[idx] (calling _ieee80211_set_tx_key unless IEEE80211_KEY_FLAG_NO_AUTO_TX) or link_sta->gtk[idx], and calls ieee80211_check_fast_rx when going from no key to a key; without a station it handles default key pointers that referred to old (clearing them when there is no new key, then storing new in sdata->keys[idx] for WEP/pairwise or link->gtk[idx], and re-pointing the defaults to new). Finally it unlinks old from the key list and returns 0.
note: Reviewer 15 right: the tailroom need count is decreased only when none of GENERATE_MMIC, PUT_MIC_SPACE or RESERVE_TAILROOM is set (key.c:515-519). Also, on a hardware-enable error the old key has already been disabled in hardware (503-509), which the old text omitted. Slice cut the head (function at 437).

name: mesh_path_timer
prose: Function mesh_path_timer(t), the timer handler of a mesh path (t is the timer embedded in the mesh_path); it returns nothing. It reads mpath->sdata and, if sdata->local->quiescing is set, returns at once without taking mpath->state_lock and without modifying mpath. Otherwise it takes mpath->state_lock (BH disabled) and exactly one branch runs: (1) if MESH_PATH_RESOLVED is set or MESH_PATH_RESOLVING is clear, it clears MESH_PATH_RESOLVING and MESH_PATH_RESOLVED and unlocks; (2) else if mpath->discovery_retries < max_preq_retries(sdata), it increments discovery_retries, doubles discovery_timeout, clears MESH_PATH_REQ_QUEUED, unlocks and calls mesh_queue_preq(mpath, 0) ignoring its result; (3) otherwise it clears MESH_PATH_RESOLVING, MESH_PATH_RESOLVED and MESH_PATH_REQ_QUEUED, sets mpath->exp_time = jiffies, unlocks, and then, if the path is not a gate and mesh_gate_num(sdata) > 0, calls mesh_path_send_to_gates(mpath) (logging a debug message if it returns non-zero), else calls mesh_path_flush_pending(mpath). The lock is released on every path.
note: Prose matches mesh_hwmp.c:1293-1326; reviewers' points (quiescing early return, resolved-flag branch, quiescing path reads mpath->sdata first) are right and already stated.

name: ieee80211_process_epcs_ena_resp
prose: Function ieee80211_process_epcs_ena_resp(sdata, mgmt, len) processing an EPCS enable response action frame; it returns nothing and takes no lock. It returns without effect if ieee80211_mgd_epcs_supp(sdata) is false. It reads the dialog token and the 16-bit status code from the frame body (the caller must supply at least IEEE80211_EPCS_ENA_RESP_BODY_LEN bytes after the action header). It returns without effect if the dialog token is 0 and either EPCS is not enabled or the status is not WLAN_STATUS_SUCCESS, or if the dialog token differs from sdata->u.mgd.epcs.dialog_token. Otherwise it sets sdata->u.mgd.epcs.dialog_token to 0 (this happens even when the status is not success); then, if the status is not WLAN_STATUS_SUCCESS it returns. It parses the remaining elements with ieee802_11_parse_elems (the parsed set is freed automatically on return); if parsing returns NULL it returns without further effect; otherwise it calls ieee80211_ml_epcs(sdata, elems) and ieee80211_epcs_changed(sdata, true).
note: Both reviewer points are right and already in the packet text: the pending dialog token is cleared before the status check (mlme.c:11104-11107), and a failed parse returns before ieee80211_ml_epcs / ieee80211_epcs_changed (11114-11119).

name: ieee80211_sta_process_chanswitch
prose: Static function ieee80211_sta_process_chanswitch(link, timestamp, device_timestamp, full_elems, csa_elems, source) processing a channel switch announcement on a managed link; the wiphy lock is held (asserted) and the function returns nothing. If csa_elems is non-NULL it WARNs and returns when link->conf->bss is NULL, otherwise it parses the CSA with ieee80211_parse_ch_switch_ie (result res; 0 fills the channel-switch parameters) and records the TPE; if csa_elems is NULL, res is 1 meaning no CSA. res < 0: an unprotected action frame is ignored (return), other sources go to drop_connection. If a CSA is already active (link->conf->csa_active): protected or unprotected action frames are ignored; for a beacon source with csa waiting_bcn it calls ieee80211_chswitch_post_beacon and then continues to the checks below (the CSA may be a new one); a beacon without waiting_bcn aborts the switch when res is non-zero, or passes the beacon to drv_channel_switch_rx_beacon when res is 0, and returns; for an other-link source it returns if the link is active, else, with waiting_bcn, completes with post_beacon and continues, else returns when res is 0 or checks the RNR for a vanished CSA (ieee80211_sta_other_link_csa_disappeared) and returns. With no new CSA (res non-zero) it clears csa.blocked_tx and unblocks the queues if blocked_tx was set, and returns. For an unprotected action frame it only blocks the queues (and sets blocked_tx) when csa_ie.mode is set, then returns. It goes to drop_connection on a different band, an unusable channel (cfg80211_chandef_usable), no channel context for an active link, a driver without CHANCTX_STA_CSA, drv_pre_channel_switch failure, or ieee80211_link_reserve_chanctx failure. If the target chandef equals the current one (and mode is 0 or the source is not a beacon) it logs once, sets csa.ignored_same_chan and returns, later times just returning. Otherwise it tears down TDLS peers (this happens before the channel-context checks), stores the new chandef, sets csa_active, clears ignored_same_chan and beacon_crc_valid, sets blocked_tx = csa_ie.mode (blocking queues when mode is set), calls cfg80211_ch_switch_started_notify, computes csa.time from the beacon count and interval, and then either calls drv_channel_switch (link active and the driver has channel_switch) or queues csa.switch_work with an hrtimer for csa.time; it returns. drop_connection sets link->conf->csa_active = true and csa.blocked_tx = csa_ie.mode and queues ifmgd->csa_connection_drop_work.
note: Reviewer 15 right: after ieee80211_chswitch_post_beacon the function does not simply return; it falls through and may process a new CSA (mlme.c:2823-2831, 2847-2855). The old prose listed those as 'does nothing'. Slice cut the head (function at 2751).

name: ieee80211_ap_power_type
prose: Static function ieee80211_ap_power_type(control): takes the HE 6 GHz operation control byte, extracts the regulatory-info field with u8_get_bits(control, IEEE80211_HE_6GHZ_OPER_CTRL_REG_INFO) (mask 0x78, bits 3 to 6, a value 0 to 15), and returns IEEE80211_REG_LPI_AP when that field is 0 (LPI AP) or 3 (indoor LPI AP), IEEE80211_REG_SP_AP when it is 1 (SP AP), 4 (old indoor SP AP) or 8 (indoor SP AP), IEEE80211_REG_VLP_AP when it is 2 (VLP AP), and IEEE80211_REG_UNSET_AP for every other value. It has no side effects.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures ((((control >> 3) & 15) == 0 || ((control >> 3) & 15) == 3) ==> result == IEEE80211_REG_LPI_AP) && ((((control >> 3) & 15) == 1 || ((control >> 3) & 15) == 4 || ((control >> 3) & 15) == 8) ==> result == IEEE80211_REG_SP_AP) && ((((control >> 3) & 15) == 2) ==> result == IEEE80211_REG_VLP_AP) && ((!((((control >> 3) & 15) == 0 || ((control >> 3) & 15) == 3 || ((control >> 3) & 15) == 1 || ((control >> 3) & 15) == 4 || ((control >> 3) & 15) == 8 || ((control >> 3) & 15) == 2))) ==> result == IEEE80211_REG_UNSET_AP); */
note: All reviewers right: the field mask is 0x78 (ieee80211-he.h:569), not 0x38, and the constants are LPI 0, SP 1, VLP 2, INDOOR_LPI 3, INDOOR_SP_OLD 4, INDOOR_SP 8 (546-551), so the old mapping (0/4 -> LPI, 1/5/6 -> SP) was wrong.
